ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the vertices of $\triangle ABC$ are all on the vertices of small squares with equal side lengths. What is the value of $\cos\angle BAC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\[ \textbf{Solution:} \text{As shown in the figure, construct } CD\perp AB \text{ at point } D, \]
\[ \text{Given that, } S_{\triangle ABC}=\frac{1}{2}\times 2\times 2=2, \quad AB=\sqrt{2^{2}+4^{2}}=2\sqrt{5}, \quad AC=2\sqrt{2}, \]
\[ \therefore S_{\triangle ABC}=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot CD=2, \quad CD=\frac{2S_{\triangle ABC}}{AB}=\frac{4}{2\sqrt{5}}=\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}, \]
\[ \text{In } \triangle ADC, \quad AD=\sqrt{AC^{2}-CD^{2}}=\frac{6\sqrt{5}}{5}, \]
\[ \therefore \cos\angle BAC=\frac{AD}{AC}=\frac{\frac{6\sqrt{5}}{5}}{2\sqrt{2}}=\boxed{\frac{3\sqrt{10}}{10}}. \]

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: on the square grid, B and C lie on the bottom horizontal grid line with C two square units to the right of B, while A lies four square units to the right and two square units above B. Count grid differences to get the three side lengths: \(BC=2\), \(AB=\sqrt{4^2+2^2}=2\sqrt5\), and \(AC=\sqrt{2^2+2^2}=2\sqrt2\). Since the required angle is at A, apply the Law of Cosines with the side opposite A being \(BC\): \(BC^2=AB^2+AC^2-2(AB)(AC)\cos A\). Thus \(\cos A=\frac{AB^2+AC^2-BC^2}{2AB\cdot AC}=\frac{20+8-4}{2(2\sqrt5)(2\sqrt2)}=\frac{24}{8\sqrt{10}}=\frac{3\sqrt{10}}{10}\).
